children: creditors are pushing the company’s main shareholders to provide fresh capital after rejecting a proposed debt restructuring,
reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Tensions in talks to restructure Braskem’s roughly $11B debt pile escalated after the company’s controllers, Petrobras
and IG4 Capital, softened the language around a potential capital injection, according to the report.

Braskem’s latest proposal, presented in late August, calls for creditors to provide about $2B in new money. Of that, $1.25B would be used to repurchase existing debt for up to 50% of face value, while $750M would go toward working capital, the report said. The proposal represents a shift from earlier discussions that did not include a debt haircut.
Creditors are demanding an enforceable commitment from shareholders, with some making clear there would be no deal without a capital injection. Petrobras
, as the company is formally known, wants to avoid having Braskem
file for bankruptcy but has been unwilling to provide the type of enforceable capital commitment sought by creditors, the people said.
The sides remain far apart, with some creditors considering not submitting a counterproposal at all. The possibility of a bankruptcy filing has consequently returned prominently to the discussions.

title: Braskem creditors shun debt proposal, press owners for cash injection - report
